Utilizing soft x-ray light-shift resonant scattering to measure the size of charge-coupled device (CCD) fabrication process variations in their early development stage, a single measurement was found to correlate with the focus depth, enabling the elimination of multiple trial-and-error methods for determining the optimal process conditions.

We introduce a novel mixed finite element method for single-phase Darcy flow through a fractured, porous medium, where the geometry consists of two distinct geometries - a complex, highly permeable network of fractures and a matrix of low permeability. The complex geometry is accurately modeled using a surface mesh, whereas a given, simple geometry is employed for the matrix with the fractures treated as interfaces within this geometry. The innovative approach described here involves locally reconstructing the matrix geometry around each individual fracture, transforming it into a prism-like geometry where the complex, highly permeable network of fractures forms the base of this new geometry. The surface finite element method is employed to discretize the complex, highly permeable network of fractures, whereas a standard piecewise constant approximation is used for the reconstructed matrix geometry. The local discretization error resulting from this approach is rigorously analyzed in this research, demonstrating its reduced impact on the approximation of the pressure.

Overcoming obstacles in adopting Bayesian techniques in various fields remains challenging, particularly due to the skepticism surrounding Bayes factors. Many Bayesian approaches now incorporate data replication or rejection steps to address concerns about Bayes factors being influenced by data fluctuations. Although these strategies align with the Bayesian framework, a systematic exploration of more robust Bayesian methods based on the removal of individual observations has not yet been conducted. This research proposes multiple Bayesian alternatives to discarding entire datasets, incorporating approaches that: (i) exclude a single data point from the current and subsequent analyses, adhering strictly to the Bayesian paradigm; (ii) incorporate stepwise procedures that incorporate p-values into the Bayesian paradigm; and (iii) integrate stepwise methods based on Bayes factors within the Bayesian paradigm. To effectively apply these strategies in practical scenarios, proposed Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms are developed and a case study utilizing real data is conducted using the Stan software, employing Stan's built-in MCMC rejection mechanism.

Social communication includes the use of discourse markers (DMs), which convey emotions and attitudes, but individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often struggle to interpret them. In this study, an emotional understanding benchmark for DMs is created to evaluate and enhance AI models' capacity to grasp the underlying meaning of these cues. This examination focuses on three prevalent DMs that convey deliberateDM, incidentalDM, and conversational management functions, each carrying different levels of semantic emotion. The research proposes a comprehensive emotional analysis framework consisting of ten dimensions, and resulting data is made available publicly. The submitted paper outlines the experimental results, showcasing that DMs with deliberateDM and conversational management categories generally convey more explicit semantic emotions than those with incidentalDM functions, which are typically neutral. The examination emphasizes the significance of implicit DM categories that are often neglected, and current employments of DMs in interpreting spoken and written language's underlying meaning are reviewed. The limitations of the study are identified and conversation-based DMs are distinguished from other categories with the same name. The dataset's examination methods and structural details are outlined in this study's context.

We examine a general category of nonconvex matrix/decompositional optimizations comprising all loss functions that are decreasing along the manifold of fixed-rank matrices. By applying a geodesically convex framework to these optimizations within the space of full-rank matrices, we discover a fundamental property: complete absence of spurious critical points. We define geodesic convexity, establish its key global landscape characteristics, and present an efficient test to determine its presence. Our analysis reveals that loss functions adhering to this nonconvex geodesic convexity have been extensively studied, but those that do not have been analyzed in depth until now. We find that standard nonconvex matrix/decompositional optimization problems, including those with (block) coordinate descent loss structures, enjoy this form of nonconvex geodesic convexity, as well as methods utilizing positivity or singular value constraints. From a numerical perspective, we propose a novel approach to tackle a broad spectrum of matrix/decompositional optimization problems by developing loss functions within the nonconvex geodesic convex framework. We also provide an in-depth analysis of the standard approach's loss functions, demonstrating their adherence to this framework. Our findings establish nonconvex geodesic convexity as a pivotal property facilitating theoretical analysis of standard matrix rank methods. We provide a comprehensive discussion on how the nonconvex geodesic convex framework relates to conventional convex and geodesic convex definitions, highlighting its broader, more strategic scope.

Burnstein and Togni recently proved a secure edge-coloring rule for cubic bipartite graphs with non-overlapping edges and triangles, giving a 5-color scheme. While working on extending this work, we are investigating the difficulty of coloring these graphs securely and achieving a four-color scheme, which seems unattainable in certain cubic bipartite graphs under the same level of safety conditions.

We employed coevolutionary genetic algorithms in a range of Cournot games to evaluate various learning algorithms in reaching a Nash equilibrium and stabilizing strategies over time. Our findings show that all methods tested successfully reached the Nash equilibrium production level and maintained it throughout the game. Our experiments also evaluated the robustness of learned strategies when pitted against new players in an out-of-sample game, our results highlighting the superior performance of a specific coevolutionary setup known as the multi-population scheme with tournament selection and random team mate.

Given a weighted directed graph, we examine the typical and symbolic powers of its edge ideal in this work, and establish the equality of typical and symbolic ideal powers for all positive integers in the case of specific directed structures.

Deep learning models, particularly those employing pattern recognition, are vulnerable to artificial hardware malfunctions caused by issues like memory errors and hardware defects, which can lead to incorrect predictions. While previous research primarily focused on software-induced errors, this work investigates the potential risks posed by hardware failures to neural network robustness. The paper develops a formal case, known as a safety case, to demonstrate the reliability of an approach called Activation Range Supervision in preventing harmful neural misclassifications. The case argues that by monitoring and maintaining the predefined operating ranges of each neuron, this method ensures safe network behavior under various hardware failure scenarios, including memory address errors, data corruption, memory flips, and memory shifts. Furthermore, the proposed solution incorporates real-time, low-overhead hardware monitoring to enhance the detection and prevention of misclassifications. The paper concludes by discussing the implications of our findings for the fields of neural network robustness and resilience.

We identify the optimal Jordanian twist for the quantized special positive $t$-Manin matrix within the quantized enveloping algebra of a Euclidean Lie algebra over the noncommutative polynomial algebra, establishing key properties such the 2-cocycle characteristic. By analyzing one-parameter deformations of the $t$-Manin matrix through the lens of the Euclidean Lie algebra's quantized enveloping algebra, we establish a structural theorem and derive a comprehensive one-parameter family of 1-parameter deformed Twisted Jordanian twist families, further validated through the example of the $q$-Manin matrix and its associated $gl_n$ quantized enveloping algebra twist, demonstrating our findings' relevance to $q$-TST.

Clustering is commonly applied within a single domain, yet it remains a challenging task across multiple domains, particularly when constructing a multi-lingual common semantic area. The incorporation of language-specific identifiers in interlingual clusters poses difficulties due to the lack of established methods for cluster translation. Our research demonstrates the feasibility of establishing a tri-lingual area encompassing English, German, and French data clusters based on their respective word embeddings. The proposed two-step procedure involves: 1) generating a domain-neutral common semantic area using a cluster-consistent technique that leverages the universal properties of word embeddings; 2) constructing language-specific interlingual areas through neural translation models trained on this common semantic area. The efficacy of our approach has been validated through the use of a benchmark consisting of random cross-lingual area constructions, with quantitative and qualitative assessments highlighting its superior performance in terms of clustering quality and ease of comprehension.

The L3 beamline is known for efficiently producing mesons and antiprotons in high-energy nuclear collisions. To investigate the conditions within these collisions, we studied a specific set of 838 Xe-Xe collisions at 5.44 TeV, focusing on pions, kaons, protons, and $\phi$ mesons. By studying the characteristics of long-range correlations and particle distributions, we explored possible signatures of quark gluon plasma formation. Additionally, a deeper analysis was conducted on short-range interactions and collective behavior, investigating possible signs of quark recombination or fluid expansion. The results showed increased collective effects in heavier nucleus collisions, but offered no clear evidence for quark recombination or the formation of quark gluon plasma in this energy range for these specific collisions.

In late October 2019, violent demonstrations swept through Chile's capital and other major cities, fueled by widespread discontent with the country's constitution, its government, and its socio-economic system. These protests, which resulted in significant property damage and the tragic loss of life, were a catalyst for the Chilean people to call for fresh democratic elections and a revised constitution. A stochastic cellular automaton model, incorporating both deterministic and stochastic elements, was developed to simulate and predict the geographical spread of the 2019 protests in Santiago de Chile. The model accounted for various influences, including sociodemographic factors and the transmission of unrest across the city. Its accuracy was validated by comparing the simulated outcomes with the actual protest locations recorded by the Chilean government, as well as by examining the temporal dynamics of the protests. Furthermore, an epidemiological interpretation of the model was proposed to better understand its mechanics.

This research aims to develop an algorithm for determining if a given regular expression, extended with the intersection operation, containing specific characters will recognize a particular word. We begin by formulating this problem symbolically, creating a congruence rewriting system to solve it efficiently, even for large and complex regular expressions with a significant number of states. Our system demonstrates significant performance improvements over existing solutions, particularly in efficiently resolving problems involving the intersection operator.

Mobile agents require accurate localization for effective navigation and localization failures can lead to navigation errors with potential safety risks. Mobile agents are prone to localization failures due to various circumstances, and we investigate the impact of dead reckoning and monocular deep learning localization methods on the localization performance of an agent. Both methods utilize inertial sensors for short-term localization and a single-camera for longer distances, and we found that they produce complementary results based on sensor accuracy and environmental conditions. However, each produces an excessive number of position errors that require extensive, inefficient optimization to address. We developed a deep learning-based attention mechanism that utilizes the accounts of the two systems and their reliability, and we conducted a meticulous examination of combined dead reckoning and monocular deep learning results and our approach's performance, and we obtained accurate localized data for training the model. We integrated our model into the deep visual localization system and conducted comprehensive, real-world evaluations, and we found that it improved the average vertical, horizontal, and diagonal localization errors by 24%, 18%, and 21%, respectively, with minimal manual intervention.

A new and distinct quantum mechanical phenomenon, known as square-root higher-order Weyl points, is revealed in both theoretical analysis and experimentally observed in a non-reciprocal photonic crystal. These singularities, in contrast to traditional WHOWP counterparts, lack local helicity, arise from the non-tri-Hermitian nature of the system, and serve as topological chargess that can be utilized to explain non-trivial photonic non-reciprocal bulk-edge correspondence. Through combination of band inversion mechanisms and the helical band-structure effect, researchers were able to observe non-trivial non-reciprocal bulk-edge correspondence in an experimentally realized non-reciprocal photonic crystal.

This study investigates the numerical resolution of a completion problem for given data in the context of the time-varying electromagnetic field. A hybrid approach, combining the quasi-reversibility method with an iterative technique known as the alternating direction implicit method, is employed to solve a highly non-smooth boundary value problem resulting from applying a specific norm. Demonstrative and supportive results obtained through numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the effectiveness and accuracy of this approach.

In this work, we address the challenge of knowledge growth across decentralized devices in two different scenarios: when data is shared between them and when additional information is collected centrally. Our focus is on designing efficient algorithms and analyzing their performance guarantees for this knowledge exchange process in a decentralized setting. We model this process called Federated Selective Collection (FSC). In the context of FSC, we develop methods for multiple agents to individually decide what information to contribute to a collective pool, achieving results comparable to a single entity with access to all data. Our solutions for graph classification and recommendation systems achieve transfer rates of close to one to one with diminishing returns, specifically $O(\log^{2.5}(\frac{T}{\epsilon}))$ and $O(\log^{3.5}(\frac{T}{\epsilon}))$ for any desired accuracy within a given time period T. Furthermore, we propose an innovative approach to collaborative learning in a cloud environment, where agents' individual data sets are used to refine a model for a distinct task, yielding improvements measured in utility gains of $1/(d\epsilon)$, where $d$ represents the dimensionality of the model being trained.

We've identified over 600 quadratic-D negative imaginary quadratic fields, denoted as K, with the property that the rank of certain elliptic curves, specifically t^3 + Dt^2 + (4K - 3) with coefficients in the ring of integers of Q, remains unchanged when raised to the 4th power. This means the rank of these curves does not increase in all 4th power extensions of Q, as demonstrated by their Galois group remaining within S_4. As far as we're aware, this is the first time such significant numbers of ranked-stable G_4 = S_4 or A_4 quartic fields, denoted as F, have been established. Additionally, this research allows us to revise the records for the count of A_4 and S_4 quartic fields up to a magnitude of 10^12, previously set at 8,160,000.

We investigate the rate of change of entanglement in a spatial interval within a two-dimensional holographic quantum field state, focusing on dynamically evolving scenarios. By leveraging the holographic dual, we derive a bound expressed as a lower limit on the second derivative of entanglement entropy with respect to the spatial interval, denoted as d²S(EA) / dδ² ≥ 2c/3χ², where c represents the central charge, χ signifies the conformal dimension, and δ indicates the dimensionless distance from the boundary of the AdS space. We analyze several distinct gravitational duals, including a sudden matter infall that creates Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime, the evolution toward AdS tilting, and the growth of a bubble within AdS. Entanglement is found to either increase, decrease, or remain unchanged, leading to intriguing interpretations of the quantum extremal surface bound and its relationship to non-locality and holographic inequalities. Moreover, we study the worst-case scenarios, where we determine the minimum possible entropy change and its associated entanglement fluctuation, revealing insights into the dynamics of holographic quantum systems.

The concept of distinguishability durations embodies the inherent uncertainty in determining whether a quantum system is in a specified target state or one of its alternative states. In a recent study, the researchers develop a methodology to create a definitive metric for the distance between two general qubit states based on their respective decoherence durations. This metric, denoted as D-hbar, enables the identification of the direction of the fundamental asymmetry within the Brouck's ball and consequently explains the origin of the inherent decoherence in the system. Notably, D-hbar accurately reflects the difference between the axial and transverse components of decoherence, and it surpasses other existing limits, including the newly devised qubit decoherence speed limit, which is proportional to the square root of the product of the angular frequencies associated with the relaxation of the z-axis and the transverse x-y axes.

Interpo projectors are linear mappings that maintain the same or improved norm of a given function or vector while working effectively with certain aspects of a specific space's structure, such as its geometric properties or the norm. This paper assesses the assessment of Norm for a specific Interpo projector defined for Hilbert space, characterized by its reliance on the arithmetic mean in defining the same. The evaluation considers multiple scenarios and compares the Interpo projector's norm to that of another established method, known as the Oblique projector, ultimately seeking to determine the exact value of this norm through the analysis of specific Hilbert spaces, including $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, $\ell_\infty$, and their subspaces.

Superconducting quantum circuits are emerging as prominent platforms for quantum computing. For practical applications, it is essential to address material defects causing quantum bit errors. This study employs terahertz Scanning Near-field Optical Microscopy to investigate the local dielectric characteristics of resonators made from aluminum and sapphire in near-field mode. TeraSANS scanning of an aluminum coplanar waveguide microwave resonator reveals strong terahertz absorption at the aluminum electrodes and transmission above the frequency plasma edge in the sapphire substrate. Notably, terahertz nanoscopy indicates that the dielectric loss in sapphire increases significantly near pattern edges, with losses up to two orders of magnitude higher than in bulk material. This finding suggests that etched chips exhibit substantially more therahz absorption than bulk samples, which could explain discrepancies between theoretical predictions and实测 results in various quantum experiments.

This paper examines the complex evolution of Venus's atmosphere over geological timeframes, focusing on both rapid and gradual atmospheric changes driven by various interactions and feedback loops. It explores how different atmospheric and surface components influenced each other, highlighting the role of CO2, water vapor, and other gases in the atmosphere, as well as the impact of the ground, volcanic activity, and cloud formations. The role of sulfuric acid aerosols and lightning in geological processes is also discussed, along with the scientific methods and theories used to understand the atmosphere of Venus.

Point process models are highly valued in analyzing datasets comprising event-based data from various domains, including our research, financial markets, and geological occurrences.  At the core of these models, parameters are established to analyze straightforward models like Poisson processes, but more intricate models are required to capture the self-influencing nature of events seen in certain datasets, exemplified by nonlinear Hawkes process.  One such example is the stock market, where past trades of a particular stock can impact future trades of the same stock.  Despite their potential, applying non-linear Hawkes processes in a Bayesian framework is challenging due to the difficulty in calculating the posterior distribution.  Our approach uses a particle filter to perform Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation and calculate integrated steps accurately for estimating the parameters of these processes.  The validity of our method is demonstrated through analysis of synthetic and real-world data, specifically the stock trading data of Apple Inc.'.

As short laser pulses become shorter and carry higher energies, the fundamental limits being explored through plasma physics are rapidly expanding, the research community is being drawn towards the study of extreme conditions, the research into sub-picosecond wavelengths and electron volt ranges is seeing unprecedented growth. The research highlights the potential applications of laser-plasma interactions across multiple promising areas, including the generation of high-energy photons, the creation of intensely polarized lasers and the production of-petawatt electron beams. The research proposes the use of non-linear processes in plasma to achieve the simultaneous improvement of polarization and power in high-energy laser pulses, the results are expected to be relevant for the exploration of new frontiers in plasma physics.

Quantum Electrodynamics predicts that a charged particle, specifically a tau lepton in this context, possesses an electric dipole quantity which can be characterized by the dimensionless parameter $d_\tau$. According to the most stringent existing constraint from the TASSO collaboration, this parameter is limited to less than $61 \times 10^{-16}~\mathrm{e}$ at the 95% confidence level. 

In this study, new limits on the tau lepton's electric dipole quantity are calculated based on decay data from the mark III, CLEO, SLD, DELCO, OPAL, ALEPH, and CDF collaborations. These calculations result in more stringent limits compared to previous findings, specifically based on results from the opal collaboration (limit $24 \times 10^{-16}$), the cleo collaboration (limit $39 \times 10^{-16}$), and the alevph collaboration (limit $42 \times 10^{-16}$), each derived at the 95% confidence level. Furthermore, combining data from all mentioned collaborations yields an even more precise limit of $23 \times 10^{-16}$ at the 95% confidence level.

We investigate the efficient decoding of rank-metric codes under the assumption that code symbols are encoded with a large number of bits, which we model using the $b$-ERank metric. This metric combines the standard Hamming distance and the logarithm of the size of the code field. Our main contribution is a decoding algorithm that can correct any rank error, whose support is within the support of a correctable hybrid error with the same weight. Furthermore, we present an alternative algorithm with different efficiency characteristics. Our methods were experimentally tested on the Goppa code, viewed as a subset of Euclidean codes, and our best performing algorithm outperformed the existing decoding approach for these codes.

Building on recent progress, we explore conformal block calculations in CFT$_2$, focusing on admissible operator contributions during adS$_3$/CFT$_2$ exchanges. Notable results from long-range AdS$_3$ field theory analyses are found, including equations for admissible four-point correlations involving quadruplets of double-trace operators. We establish constraints on the AdS$_3$ amplitude of closed quartic interactions based on the positivity of adS conformal block calculations. Furthermore, we demonstrate the usefulness of adS$_3$/CFT$_2$ consistency checks by validating recent findings on admissible AdS$_3$ gravity theories with higher-spin symmetries, W$_{\infty}[\lambda]$ in particular. Finally, we derive novel structures for admissible OPE blocks in CFT$_2$ with leading-order quartic operators, verify the results from Batlle et al., and derive an adS$_3$ gravity equation for these models with W$_{\infty}[\lambda]` symmetry, demonstrating its equivalence to Fefferman–Graham expansions.

In 1992, D. S. Dummit generalized the combinatorial formula for Pontrjagin classes originally developed by Gelfand and MacPherson. We restore the full context of the Z4_graded_cohomology ring expansion, generalizing Dummit's combinatorial equation to a broader setting.

We combined previous and new data to analyze the optical spectrum and light variation of SN 2020jfo, which is associated with a star-forming region and classified as a hydrogen-rich Type II supernova with a short plateau duration. Based on comparisons with other SN II-pec subtypes, we placed SN 2020jfo in the SN II category. Observations placed its host galaxy, located 20.6 megaparsecs away, and revealed the peak absolute magnitude in the V band as -17.2. Observations initially indicated the remnant was rotating at 200 km/s but this decreased to 140 km/s three days later, a pattern typical of SN II spectra. However, the total hydrogen output of $4.55 \times 10^{49}$ atoms was unusually high for a SN II with a short plateau, which also had an unusually long tail in its light variation that was longer than observed in similar SN II-nec subtypes. The amount of 542 solar masses in the examined galaxy is also noted.

To extensively cover the sky in X-rays with high sensitivity, constructing large detectors is challenging. Our research demonstrates how to create a multiplexed system of 64 mini detectors, each employing a unique lobster-eye optical design, arranged in a hexagonal pattern to cover an area of 25 square steradians. These designs are characterized by their superior focusing abilities, wide viewing angles, and uniform distribution of sensitivity. Our study analyzes a potential application for this multiplexed system in high-frequency X-ray monitoring, highlighting its capability to detect small sources of X-rays across the sky, located various distances from the system, either directly or indirectly. Our analysis also provides simulated images of the system's view and identifies the ideal system configuration for monitoring astronomical phenomena.

We establish a level set formulation for partial uniform ellipticity with non-negative concave functions f, where the semi-convexity order is employed. This method allows us to apply previous results and resolve new problems. Specifically, when considering the p-Laplace equation or a quasi-convex version for u in Omega, a ball Om radius h contains points where the convex hull of u's D^2_u behavior is non-empty, or its concave hull is at least 2p-Omega for some positive constant C. This implies that for a permutation sigma of {1,...,k}, there is a concentration of curvature where the sum of convexities or concavities over radius h is Atotal / h^k for constants A, B. These properties hold for u in solutions to the p-Laplace equation or a quasisymmetric variant in Omega. Moreover, from the level set ellipticity, we derive regularity estimates, including local boundedness, continuity, and a gradient estimate for u, where at some points, u exhibits a certain degree of convexity or concavity based on the parameters of the equation and a given constant theta, or remains within a concave envelope for a given radius h.

Lamport's theory posits that the growth of structure in the universe is position-dependent, particularly in relation to the speed of particles. By positioning the speed of neutrons as a cosmic field and incorporating it into N-body simulations, significant results were achieved in modeling phenomena such as halo formation. To gain a deeper understanding of how halos form in relation to the speed field, deep learning methodologies were employed to examine N-body simulations of dark matter. It was discovered through these analyses that deep learning models could effectively predict the halo mass function based on two key parameters: the halo's linear density perturbation and the local speed of dark matter. Furthermore, the model used regression trees to differentiate between halo collapse modes, including those driven by shear and radial pressure, based on the velocity dispersion and speed of dark matter within them. As a consequence, significant enhancements were made in predicting the halo formation probability within underdense regions of the universe, thereby extending the halo collapse model through the application of deep learning.

We have developed a new numerical approach for creating rotating star models in the context of general relativity. This method uses a specific type of mathematical basis functions to directly formulate the equations governing the stars in a new, non-orthogonal coordinate system. This coordinate system is tailored to the nature of stars, where the angular momentum is aligned with one of the axes, angular position is defined by a periodic angle, and both the angular momentum and radial distance are discrete quantities. By choosing basis functions that satisfy these boundary conditions, we found that we can reduce the number of unknown variables and improve numerical stability. This method has been successfully used to create models of rotating stars, especially those influenced by strong magnetic and magnetic-boosonans fields, in both classical and general relativistic settings. Our approach offers numerical advantages over previous methods in solving the radial part of the problem in settings with general relativity and a boosonans field.

Existing document extraction models, such as LayoutLM, are rich in visual information but heavily rely on heavily labeled data, which is costly and impractical in many cases. This work explores a scenario where only the functional requirements and unannotated, unstructured documents are available. We introduce two new challenges that reflect this situation: Document Compliance Detection (DCD) and Visually Rich Document Answering (VRDA). To tackle these challenges cost-effectively, our model, called Positive Label Free Document Understanding (PLFDU), leverages the often-overlooked supervision from rejection samples. Instead of traditional fully supervised training, our model uses a reductionist fully supervised approach, labeled-free embedding pretraining, and positive label free label pretraining (PLFLL) strategies. Our experimental results show that PLFDU achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art fully supervised baseline on two publicly available documents datasets (DocVQA and SDOCQA) with significantly lower data-labeling costs.

The discovery of neutron star-neutron star mergers that produce gravitational waves has opened up a new area of research for multi-messenger astronomy. To detect these events effectively, it is crucial to research how neutron star-disruption with black holes releases electromagnetic radiation. Neutron star-disruption can sometimes result in short-duration gamma-ray bursts and associated afterglows, which are highly detectable by current instruments. However, training machine learning models using only simulated data to identify these events has yielded inaccurate results due to incomplete knowledge of the gamma-ray data catalog. In this study, we developed a two-step approach to identify and classify neutron star-black hole events by utilizing only the Gravitational Wave data from the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog. Our models can distinguish NS-BH events and classify their spin properties with spin-spin correlations in a short amount of time. But they also found that many of the potential gamma-ray events originate from the middle of the NS-BH merger timeline, which could challenge existing theories.

Urban environments are known to promote diverse interactions among individuals from various income backgrounds through face-to-face contact within cities. However, the limitations imposed by COVID-19 in cities have hindered this beneficial aspect of urban living. Researchers investigated how COVID-19 affected social interactions between people of different income levels in urban settings. A data analysis was conducted on mobile phone movements in the city of Zurich, Switzerland, revealing significant changes in social encounters during the pandemic. These findings indicated that during the pandemic, diversity of income backgrounds in urban social interactions declined substantially. A mathematical model further supported this discovery. The study found that the decrease in social interactions due to COVID-19 played a crucial role in reducing the diversity of income backgrounds in encounters. Additionally, changes in behavior led to an increase in segregation according to economic status. If researchers' estimates regarding COVID-19-related behavior are accurate, they could have temporary but substantial impacts on the diversity of social interactions within urban environments globally.

We used the SPH-Gr thermodynamic solver to investigate how the accumulation of gas in massive protostars' gravitational wells affects their growth and interactions. Our simulations covered three different mass accumulation scenarios: continuous accretion, a common model, and two distinct episodes of accretion pauses. Results show that accretion stoppages significantly influence the formation of massive protostars, especially in relation to their size, which is further affected by a variety of factors including: accretion density, dispersion rates, episode duration, and frequency. In most cases, we found that accretion episodes lead to the buildup of gas around the protostar, which eventually disperses through a type II shock, frequently causing a short-lived outflow. We also observed that accretion episodes can lead to the accumulation of gas that leads to protostar-protostar interactions and mergers, a process rarely seen with a model of constant accretion. Our findings suggest that accretion episodes could be an unrecognised source of mergers among young massive clusters and could leave traces in the star cluster formation history.

This research extends our previous work, which established the Hamiltonian Dysthe equation in its form without circulation for water waves, focusing on the inclusion of constant water circulation. By applying a near-resonant, long-wave approximation to the surface integral of the nonlinear Hamiltonian, we derived the Dysthe equation in its form with circulation. We then compared it to variants developed through direct time evolution linearization, and found that while they share similar characteristics, they diverge in terms of linear frequencies and Hamiltonian properties. Ultimately, we determined that each of these versions can be viewed as specialized instances of the Dysthe equation with circulation, and proposed its irreducible, general form.

In this work, a new concept called differential p-forms is introduced in the context of a specific mathematical structure known as a smooth space over a commutative smooth algebra P. These forms extend the traditional differential p-forms when P is the set of real numbers. A key property of these forms, which generalizes the well-known Stokes formula, is established. Additionally, specific scenarios are examined where the introduced forms coincide with the standard differential forms.

This research focuses on creating a navigation system for an autonomous aircraft using sonar sensors and a PID controller in order to follow a path defined by various layers. Sonar sensors were selected due to their cost-effectiveness and ease of integration with the Arduino platform, despite having higher noise levels compared to other alternatives such as LiDAR. A navigation strategy based on layered control was implemented and tested using Gazebo and MATLAB for simulation and control parameter tuning respectively. In this study, sonar sensors were integrated into the input of a virtual camera to guide the aircraft along a path with turns in both directions. Experimental results show that the autonomous aircraft can successfully follow defined navigation layers using this system.

The prevalence of false news on the internet is rapidly escalating, posing a significant issue. Researchers are exploring various solutions to counter this problem, including automated methods. This study evaluates whether conventional text processing techniques can effectively identify false news. Specifically, we investigate if Constrained Sentence Embedding (CSEE) can be utilized for this purpose. To enhance the performance of CSEE in identifying false news, we applied three different topics obtained from Twitter tweets to incorporate external knowledge. Furthermore, we compared the results with other state-of-the-art approaches. Our evaluations were conducted on three widely recognized fake news datasets from TFAF.org. Our empirical evidence reveals that CSEE achieves comparable performance to other leading methods. However, our performance lags behind other high-performance approaches such as using Graph Convolutional Networks on Twitter retweet graphs or employing rule-based systems. Interestingly, our research also discovered that leveraging external knowledge did not yield positive outcomes. Additionally, our study found that simple text preprocessing methods can effectively identify false news posted on Twitter.

This research investigates the influence of a positive correlation structure on the stochastic behavior of Gaussian random fields, specifically focusing on an excursion probability of interest exceeding a given threshold level. A striking observation is made, where the interest level is below one unit of variance and is referred to as the bending effect. A mathematical expression is derived to describe the variance level at which this effect occurs in relation to spatial range and dimensionality of the random field. A distinct characteristic is noted, where the excursion probability of interest staying below the threshold level initially widens before narrowing beyond the identified variance level. A simulation model is developed and utilized to verify the research findings, where it is demonstrated that after the bending effect, interest level behaves like in independent random field cases. Various statistical control charting methods are explored to further illustrate the bending effect.

We examine the $\ell_1$-norm PCA problem under conditions where it is not convex, focusing on data that exhibits rotational symmetry. This study aims to develop a simplified, optimal algorithm with Conjugate Gradient variations to solve such problems, specifically adapting to manifolds. Our method, when applied to flat spaces, matches a known Conjugate Frank-Wolfe approach but demonstrates improved performance and efficiency by leveraging manifold properties to reduce computational efforts and improve numerical precision. Numerical experiments show that our algorithm outperforms existing methods in both speed and accuracy by a significant margin, particularly when dealing with large datasets, as it combines the benefits of Riemannian RLR and FR algorithms with a manifold-based variation of Conjugate Direction methods.

The rapid expansion of the internet has significantly increased the amount of unstructured textual data, creating a demand for efficient and reliable methods to annotate the semantics of questions asked by users. Traditional annotation approaches rely on predefined templates and knowledge bases, but these methods are limited when it comes to processing the vast amounts of unstructured content generated on the internet. A novel research proposed in this paper aims to improve the accuracy of semantic annotations for questions with expressed emotions, by utilizing the Emotion Knowledge Base and an Emotion Question dataset that was created to evaluate the effectiveness of a new approach. The research tested two methods for converting questions into semantic labels, including a traditional keyword extraction technique and a technique based on BERT, with the latter showing a 20% higher level of effectiveness in terms of average label accuracy compared to the former. Emotion Question data was also discovered to be approximately 20% harder to convert into accurate semantic labels than non-emotional questions.

A significant challenge in autonomous navigation is moving through unfamiliar surroundings. Knowledge of the environment is essential for this task. Learning from demonstrations is a popular approach to acquire environment information. However, existing methods struggle with generalizing to unfamiliar parts of the environment due to their simple, flat representations that fail to capture the environment's complex structure. In this work, we investigate a more expressive, hierarchical graph representation of the environment. We introduce HiTMap, a method representing the environment as a hierarchical graph, where a subgraph is a detailed local feature, and connections to other nodes provide an abstract, global context. We employ reinforcement learning to efficiently and effectively train the hierarchical graph representation. We evaluate our method in unknown environments, comparing it with current state-of-the-art learning-based representations, and our results show that HiTMap provides a more effective navigation strategy in unfamiliar environments.

One of the key challenges in atomic interference metrology is accurately accounting for the impact of local magnetic field fluctuations on precision and correctness of measurements. Although researchers have utilized laser cooling and atomic micro-cavitors to effectively counteract noise from varying local magnetic fields, there is still a lack of in-depth studies on the fundamental characteristics of these fluctuations. By employing atomic interference measurements, we developed a method to map the complex local magnetic field environment, demonstrating that non-uniform magnetic fields create distinct, location-specific signatures that can be clearly identified through a simple experiment. This approach was effectively validated by theoretical models, numerical simulations, and the non-uniform Meissner effect exhibited in superconducting plates.

This note establishes a bridge between the theory of finite mixture models in statistics and two related mathematical fields: convex geometry and Choquet theory. We demonstrate how a specific type of probability distributions, known as finite mixture models, can be linked to convex hulls and the set of simplicial measures. Furthermore, we discuss the fundamental decomposition of a given measure within a prescribed class of measures, a crucial problem in a variety of statistical applications.

High-performance graph processing on GPUs is hindered by the object-based programming paradigm's heavy overhead from memory access. Researchers are proposing modified graph representations to optimize performance, but these changes deviate significantly from the original data structure, making them difficult to integrate into existing code. Our new parallel memory allocation system, DynaSOAr, automatically allocates memory for objects according to a user-defined adjacency list, placing connected nodes closer together in memory to improve cache efficiency and reduce data movement. DynaSOAr uses multiple allocator threads to distribute the workload and minimize GPU memory access time, achieving up to 2.4x faster graph traversal and 1.6x better performance in object-dependent applications compared to the industry-standard allocator CuObject.

A comprehensive, first-principles, relativistic theory is developed for Yu--Shiba--Rusinov states, serving as an essential tool in designing nanomagnetic devices. Our analysis of Mn adatom and Mn dimer/trimer/tetramer clusters on semi-infinite Nb(110) surface reveals that all states associated with the Mn 3d $t_{2g}$-derived minority-spin bands are occupied, rendering sMR state manipulation via cluster geometry changes impractical in this system.

The TOI-712 star is home TOI-712 b and c, two highly characterised exoplanets with orbital periods of 6.6 days and 20.4 days respectively, under the study of which Li et al. (2023) originally reported TOI-712 b and later identified TOI-712 c using combined analyses of their light curve. TOI-712 b and c, both possessing similar properties, are found to be in a 2:5 mean motion resonance, and reside within the inner edge of TOI-712's habitable zone. Researchers have categorised the population of Neptune-sized planets into four sub-populations based on their semi-major axes relative to their habitable zone inner edge, to which TOI-712 b and c are found to belong the outermost of which. TOI-712 b and c, being only around 25 million years of age, are among the youngest mini-Neptunes ever discovered, and occupy a previously unexplored section of mini-Neptune parameter space, and to directly image which astronomers will need to consider the effects that TOI-712 b and c would have on any direct images obtained of possible TOI-712 Earth-like planets.

We investigate the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of carbon and nitrogen defects in carbon dioxide-doped rutile TiO2 through structural relaxations, using relativistic density functional theory within the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method. Carbon and nitrogen show sp3 hybridization in d0 and d1 configurations with significant hybridization around -2 to 2 eV, exhibiting localized states with corresponding atomic positions and negligible interstitial or substitutional interactions. Both show narrow and narrower bands than the valence band maximum, with a reduced or eliminated band gap, exhibiting no inter-element interactions. Both show moderate adsorption energies of -4.8 to -5.8 eV, with nitrogen showing narrow, narrow, and localized N 2s and N 2p states, with a higher work function of 4.5 to 5.5 eV, with nitrogen showing better conductivity than carbon. Both show high total effective densities of states at the Fermi level, with a preference for nitrogen defects.

A new top quark production criterion, based on the conservation of elastic energy, has been introduced. This conservation principle considers the elastic energy of incoming protons in the context of the nearly elastic scattering of protons on protons. The proposed method to hunt for the production of top quark pairs through the weak interaction allows for the top quark pair's mass to be directly calculated from the measured final state particles and the elastic energy, providing a straightforward and comprehensible way to calculate the top quark mass from an explicit final state.

We build upon the concept of graph richness introduced by Kwan, Seeger, and Sudakov, specifically the idea that a pair of triangles in a Ramsey graph can be formed by connecting three mutually disjoint edges in an infinite complete graph according to a specific pattern that avoids creating triangles. Specifically, we show that if we are given any such infinite graph and a way to color its structure similar to that of a triangle-avoiding graph, there exists a trio of edges that, when connected to form a triangle, will necessarily create a triangle. This holds true for a class of infinite graphs that includes instances where one or more of the edges are replaced with structures that have higher complexity or "richness" than the initial infinite graph, within the context of a trio of scholars exploring the properties of infinite graph theory.

Our in-depth analysis of quenched lattice scalar QED in the transverse field Ising model with qutrits reveals increased noise levels compared to previous two-level system quantum simulators. Although we rederive expected noise behavior for standard two-qubit systems, we derive and investigate noise dynamics specific to two-qudit systems in the relevant range. Experiments show proper noise propagation and scaling, but also higher noise levels than predicted, possibly due to crosstalk, providing a foundation for correcting such effects.

Research into positron physics using high-intensity lasers calls for high-density, spin-polarized positron beams. The development of such lasers necessitates the identification of efficient methods to generate high-density positrons from vacuum. Our findings demonstrate that high-intensity lasers can generate dense positron plasmas from thin metallic films when illuminated at oblique angles with moderately energetic photons. By adjusting the experiment conditions carefully, a positron plasma with a density of 10^12 cm^-3 was achieved over a small area, and a positron beam with a polarization degree of 0.6 and the same magnitude as the beam current could be produced in a subsequent process. The described mechanism and results are applicable to a wide range of future high-intensity laser experiments that require dense, polarized positron sources.

A polynomial outer automorphism growth characterizes the family of finite groups whose groups of zero-dimensionally embedded finite subgroups can be efficiently bounded by a power of the bound for embedded groups.

To facilitate the automatic calibration of analog circuits, a highly compact temperature sensor was developed to track temperature variations at the circuit's operating points or to provide visual displays of temperatures or temperature ranges. The novel sensor employs an intrinsic positive temperature coefficient resistor and an OPAMP with programmable heating capabilities to raise the ambient temperature of the device under test in discrete increments. The modified Bethe–Bloch curve is utilized to convert temperature increments to a measurable voltage signal. The sensor features an on-chip reference temperature, a range indicator, and an absolute temperature measurement capability. The designed sensor has an on-chip reference temperature, capable of displaying a temperature range indicator and measuring the absolute temperature in degrees Celsius. The developed sensor exhibits an impressive resolution of 0.24{\deg}C within an operating voltage range of 0.6 to 1.8V, with an inaccuracy of 1.4{\deg}C and a test duration of 1.1 seconds at 1.2V and a minimum temperature step size of 1.8mK. The sensor exhibits an exceptionally high level of integration, featuring a compact footprint of 0.12 mm x 0.12 mm, with the ability to accurately detect minute temperature fluctuations within a wide voltage range.

In this study, we develop key differential geometric structures within the category of Lie groupoids and equivalences, focusing on extensions, reductions, and quotients. These structures mirror familiar concepts from the geometry of manifolds and their submanifolds. Notably, we establish that reduction of Lie groupoids and their associated stacks adheres to a 2-cococycle rule, and we define and investigate open subsets, smooth functions, and vector fields on differentiable stacks.

Interstellar molecular cloud cores contract and grow more dense before the birth of stars, yet contrary evidence shows some of these cores actually expanding and that this process may lead to star formation, especially massive ones. By studying the far-infrared emissions of the Dragon IRDC using the IRAM 30m telescope, we discovered that a specific area known as 'Dragon' is expanding at a speed between 0.15 and 0.25 km/s. This expansion rate is consistent with what might be expected from turbulent motions within the cloud. We found that this expansion isn't uniform in all directions but varies depending on the angle, and it's happening despite the presence of a massive protostellar object within the cloud. The discovery of an expanding cloud core could help explain why many massive star-forming regions lack the typical dense cores and may hint at other star formation anomalies.

The Recurrence Relation (RR) approach is a well-established technique for improving Bessel basis expansions, originally formulated by Tjostheim in 1977. Three key parameters - λ, μ, and n - define the (n, λ, μ)-Stieltjes-Wigert (SW) operator, and its associated spectrum comprises three distinct components: the discrete part corresponds to the orthogonal polynomials known as Stieltjes–Christoffel–Robin (SCR), while the continuous part is comprised of two identical parts of the SW operator itself. We examine three types of Schrödinger operators called (stationary, evolving, and stagnant) SW operator Heisenberg recurrences (SWHR), denoted as (SWHR)-S, (SWHR)-E, and (SWHR)-Stag, each with their own unique set of parameters and scattering matrices. The analysis of the (n, λ, μ)-SW operator reveals that the Stag operator's parameters result in a single continuous spectrum component with scattering matrix consisting of two complex conjugate numbers of modulus unity, reflecting phase shifts.
